cards.desc: The Somali Sengi, also called the Somali Elephant-shrew, is a mouse-size African mammal with a long and flexible nose that it waggles to and fro. In fact, it is a close relative of other trunk-nosed creatures like aardvarks, elephants, and manatees.

cards.title: Lost species of fanged 'mouse deer' spotted for first time in 30 years
cards.desc: A lost species known as the silver-backed chevrotain, or the Vietnamese ‘mouse deer,’ has been caught on camera for the first time since 1990.

cards.title: FOUND: World’s Largest Bee—With Giant Jaws—Rediscovered in the Wild After 38 Years Missing
cards.desc: Search Team Produces First-ever Live Photos and Video of Indonesia’s Extraordinary Lost Bee Species.

cards.title: Citizen science leads to snail rediscovery in Vietnam
cards.desc: Scott Trageser photographed invertebrates on Hon Cau, an island off south-east Vietnam, and posted them to iNaturalist hoping somebody could identify them. In November 2015 the malacologist Junn Kitt Foon recognised one as Myxostoma petiverianum, a land snail
cards.citation: Trageser, S.J., Wiscovitch, A. & Foon, J.K. (2018) Discovery of Myxostoma petiverianum Wood, 1828 on Hon Cau, Vietnam. The Festivus 50(2): 110-113.
cards.note: Found in a photograph, not in the field: identified from an iNaturalist post more than a year after it was taken.
